state.task:
Question-answering task using the company document service.

The company handbook is held by a document service; it is not available as files. Documents
have a header line (version, status, effective dates, what they supersede) and numbered
sections; each section is a passage, cited as "HB-07 §2". Documents can have superseded
versions, and memos can add group exceptions and carve-outs. Use the rule that applies to the
situation and date in the question.

Service actions (reply with one of these instead of "execute"):
  {"action": "search", "query": "lodging limit Geneva", "k": 5, "thought": "..."}
      up to k (at most 8; default 5) ranked passages with ids and document headers. Each
      result is also saved under /task/workspace/search-results/ (path in the result header),
      where your code can read it later.
  {"action": "fetch", "ids": ["HB-07 §2", "HB-12"], "thought": "..."}
      the named passages in full; a document id ("HB-12") returns all its sections; at most
      10 ids per fetch.
You can still use "execute" for code (for example to read saved results or manage your
context), and "final" to answer.

Questions:
- Q1: What is the home-office equipment allowance for an employee with a medical accessibility plan who works 16 hours a week today? (answer in EUR)
- Q2: What is the nightly lodging limit for a business trip to Geneva today? (answer in EUR per night)
- Q3: What taxi allowance applied to a daytime business taxi ride on 2026-02-15? (answer in EUR per ride)
- Q4: What is the paid parental leave for a primary carer in their first year of employment today? (answer in weeks)
- Q5: What is the relocation lump sum for a regular employee relocating at the company's request with dependent children today? (answer in EUR)
- Q6: What is the monthly parking allowance for a regular employee driving to the office today (2026-10-13)? (answer in EUR per month)

Finish with {"action": "final", "answer": {"answers": [{"question": "Q1", "value": "...",
"citations": ["HB-07 §2", ...]}, ...]}}. Give one entry per question. The value must be the
exact amount; citations must include every passage needed to support it (for example the rule
and any exception or carve-out that applies), not just one passage.
state.query: paid parental leave primary carer first year of employment

passages.source: HB-71 §2 | Memo: paid parental leave exceptions — Exception for employees who are the primary carer | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-02-01
passages.text: For employees who are the primary carer, the paid parental leave is 19 weeks instead of the standard amount. Each claim for the paid parental leave needs a receipt showing the date, the amount and the supplier. Questions about the paid parental leave go to the HR, who keeps the record of decisions.

passages.source: HB-71 §3 | Memo: paid parental leave exceptions — Carve-out | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-02-01
passages.text: The exception above does not apply to employees in their first year of employment; they follow the standard paid parental leave in HB-06 §2. The HR reviews the paid parental leave once a year and announces changes in advance. The HR publishes worked examples of the paid parental leave on the intranet.

passages.source: HB-06 §1 | HR policy: parental leave — Scope | version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-03-01 · supersedes: HB-25
passages.text: This policy sets the paid parental leave for all employees. The HR reviews the paid parental leave once a year and announces changes in advance. Managers confirm claims for the paid parental leave before payment in the next payroll run.

passages.source: HB-06 §3 | HR policy: parental leave — Additions | version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-03-01 · supersedes: HB-25
passages.text: For parents of multiple births, 4 weeks is added to the standard paid parental leave. Questions about the paid parental leave go to the HR, who keeps the record of decisions. The HR reviews the paid parental leave once a year and announces changes in advance.

passages.source: HB-25 §2 | HR policy: parental leave — Standard paid parental leave | version: 2 · status: superseded · effective: 2025-02-01 to the day before 2026-03-01 · superseded by: HB-06
passages.text: Each parent may take 9 weeks of paid parental leave. Claims for the paid parental leave are filed in the expense tool under 'HR policy: parental leave'. Managers confirm claims for the paid parental leave before payment in the next payroll run.
